aspects.says: References are 4 bytes through compressed oops up to a 32 GB heap; from -Xmx32g the JVM turns them off and every reference field and array slot doubles, while the header stays 12 bytes.
basis: section:An Object Costs a Header Plus Its Fields, Rounded Up to 8 Bytes; a Reference Costs 4 Bytes Below 32 GB

aspects.says: -Xss decides how many frames fit, and the depth changes with frame size and JIT compilation, so a recursion as deep as its input overflows on some input while a loop or an explicit stack on the heap doesn't; a bigger -Xss only moves the limit.
basis: section:-Xss Sets How Many Frames Fit, So Recursion as Deep as the Data Fails on Large Input

aspects.says: C2's escape analysis removes the allocation of an object that provably stays local in compiled code; a field store, or a call the JIT doesn't inline, makes it escape, and HotSpot never puts the object on the stack instead.
basis: section:Escape Analysis Can Remove an Allocation, but Only in Compiled Code and Only While the Object Stays Local

aspects.says: A frame holds a call's parameters and locals, so more live locals mean fewer frames fit; an object the call creates is on the heap, and the frame holds only a reference to it.
basis: section:A Frame Holds a Call's Locals; Every Object the Call Creates Lives on the Heap
aspects.reason: where the JVM keeps a value is visible only by counting frames under -Xint, as the page does; a graded test sees the result of a call, not where its locals lived

aspects.says: Class metadata lives in Metaspace, outside -Xmx and unlimited by default; generated classes kept reachable exhaust it with the heap nearly empty, and unreachable hidden classes are unloaded.
Java has no tail-call elimination: a recursive call in the last position still pushes a frame.
basis: section:-Xss Sets How Many Frames Fit, So Recursion as Deep as the Data Fails on Large Input

aspects.says: An object costs a 12-byte header plus its fields, rounded up to 8 bytes; a Long is 24 bytes, so a list of Longs costs about 28 bytes per number against 8 in a long[].
basis: section:An Object Costs a Header Plus Its Fields, Rounded Up to 8 Bytes; a Reference Costs 4 Bytes Below 32 GB

aspects.says: OutOfMemoryError is thrown by the allocation that failed, so the trace names the victim rather than what holds the memory, and a bigger heap only moves the failure while the holder keeps growing.
basis: section:OutOfMemoryError Is Thrown by Whichever Allocation Fails, Not by the Code That Filled the Heap

aspects.says: A collection that is empty to its users but keeps references in slots it no longer reads keeps those objects reachable, so the collector can't free them.
basis: section:OutOfMemoryError Is Thrown by Whichever Allocation Fails, Not by the Code That Filled the Heap

aspects.says: A virtual thread's frames go to the heap when it unmounts, but -Xss caps its depth as it caps a platform thread's; one platform thread can get its own stack size.
basis: section:-Xss Sets How Many Frames Fit, So Recursion as Deep as the Data Fails on Large Input
